result.topic_en: An equation for finding n from the other quantities (apparently an annuity or interest problem), with a worked example tabulating n for several interest rates, followed by a list of books from 1844.
result.transcription:
Für den Fall wo $n$ aus den übrigen Größen gesucht wird ist die einfachste Form der Gleichung folgende
$1 = \frac{1}{x^n} + n\left\{\frac{(Ax - A - a)(x-1)}{Bx - A - a}\right\}$
Beispiel $A=90,\ a=3,\ B=100$
$100x - 100$ | | $n$
[-3-] | [-$\frac{100}{103}{}^n$-] |
$3\frac{1}{2}$ | $1 = \left(\frac{200}{207}\right)^n + \frac{21}{2000}\cdot n$ | $91,0904$
$4$ | $1 = \left(\frac{25}{26}\right)^n + \frac{3}{125}\cdot n$ | $27,492345$
$4\frac{1}{2}$ | $1 = \left(\frac{200}{209}\right)^n + \frac{63}{2000}\cdot n$ | $16,159$
$5$ | $1 = \left(\frac{20}{21}\right)^n + \frac{3}{80} n$ | $11.307$

methods.what: Equation for determining the number of periods n from the other quantities A, a, B and x (x = 1 + rate)
Numerical example with A=90, a=3, B=100: the equation solved for n at interest rates 3½%, 4%, 4½% and 5%
